deckTitle: Du Elender Wicht! — Ritual Insults as Performace Art
blurb: This deck is for players who treat insult as performance art, not therapy. You read cards aloud, the table judges whether they land, someone counters with their own evidence, and you keep going until the scene runs dry.
deckType: Uncle FrizzleBob’s Komik Kards for Bizarro Insults, Kayfabe Curses Karaoke & Ritual Provocations

cards.name: Uncle FrizzleBob
cards.power: Master of the Gift: Swap hands when you've been verbally outplayed.
cards.lore: He jests, he taunts. Mostly talks in riddles. Mostly practical. KayfaBIZARRO!
cards.gradeReason: Mascot instigator card—table energy starts the second he enters.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: carnival satire comic. Subject: badger showman offering cursed gift. Mood: chaotic host.

cards.name: The Schimpfgeist

cards.lore: An insult spirit. It’s practically a portable bad habit of verbal abuse. KayfaHUMBUG!
cards.gradeReason: Portable insult ghost is pure ritual ignition and instantly memorable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ghost satire comic. Subject: shouting insult spirit floating angrily. Mood: disruptive mockery.

cards.name: The Malediction

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark folklore comic. Subject: shadow curse wrapping frightened squirrel. Mood: malicious doom.

## QA

qa.verdict: This deck is not about insults—it is about ritualized social combat disguised as insults, which is much smarter. The best cards—The Provocation, Bless Your Heart, KayfaHUMBUG!—don’t describe conflict, they force it into existence. That’s the real Kayfabizarro engine. Regional slang cards are fun seasoning, but the manifesto/meta cards are the spine. Table-ready? Completely. Hide this near family gatherings and let anthropology happen.

urgent: Clean a few OCR-rough lore lines around intro and regional dialect cards for exact phrasing
quickWins: Standardize capitalization between curse cards and regional insult entries
Slightly sharpen weaker descriptive cards that explain more than they activate
niceToHave: Tiny icon consistency pass across final manifesto/flyting sequence cards

notes: Cover page and final scissors-warning page are decorative/meta framing and not counted as gameplay pages. This deck works best when treated as ritual social choreography, not balanced mechanics: insult, response, escalation, boundary. The final four cards are effectively the operating system for the entire Kayfabizarro project.
marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: DU ELENDER WICHT! – The Global Insult Kompendium (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Every culture on earth built an art form out of the insult. Yours sold you anger management instead.

Here is the assumption this deck exists to wreck: that the person who stays quiet is the bigger one. They are not the bigger one. They are just unarmed. From the Bavarian beer-table to the Shakespearean court to the Greek kafeneio, every serious culture treated the insult as a craft with rules, a back-and-forth of provocation, answer, and escalation that stops precisely where both players agree to stop. What got handed to you instead was a narrow little choice: swallow it, or lose your temper. This deck hands back the third option the rest of the world never threw away.

This is Social Story Wrestling with the gloves off and the dictionary open. 64 cut-and-play cards turn the flyting traditions of six cultures into a ritual you perform out loud, at the table, where the room decides whether your burn lands clean or snaps back in your face.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Du Elender Wicht! Core Deck: 64 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring Bless Your Heart (the Southern smile that buries a knife so politely the target thanks you for it), MALAKA (The Greek Swiss-Knife) (one word that bends from insult to endearment depending entirely on how you sell it), and KayfaHUMBUG! (the all-purpose curse you reach for when the moment is too big for any real language).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, RAF dice that decide how hard a burn lands, and the boundary beat that ends every exchange before cruelty replaces craft.
- The Flyting Engine: six insult cultures racked side by side, Bavarian, Shakespearean, Norse, Southern, Italian, and Greek, plus the four-card ritual core, insult, response, escalation, boundary, that runs this deck and quietly runs the whole Kayfabizarro project underneath it.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I keep this one in print because the ritual insult is the most honest social technology we have, and nobody else is going to defend it. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Use it. Win an argument you have been losing for years. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the next deck.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Cruelty just wants you gone. A real insult wants you to answer."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
